subject: pe
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Calcium is an important mineral for performers because it:
questions.explain: Calcium is needed for strong bones and teeth, reducing the risk of fractures.

questions.q: Mixing with others and making friends through sport is an example of which type of well-being?
questions.explain: Social well-being involves interacting with others, cooperating and forming friendships.

questions.q: Which nutrient helps the digestive system work properly and prevents constipation?
questions.explain: Dietary fibre adds bulk to food and aids the movement of food through the digestive system.

questions.q: Iron is an important mineral in the diet because it:
options: Helps form haemoglobin to carry oxygen
questions.explain: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin in red blood cells, which transports oxygen.

questions.q: Optimum weight for a performer depends on factors such as:
options: Height, sex, bone structure and muscle girth
questions.explain: Optimum weight varies between individuals according to height, sex, bone structure and muscle girth.

questions.q: Which of these is a benefit of regular physical activity for physical health?
options: Reduced risk of coronary heart disease
questions.explain: Regular exercise strengthens the heart and reduces the risk of coronary heart disease.

questions.q: Which performer is most likely to benefit from an endomorph somatotype?
questions.explain: Endomorphs carry more body mass, which can be an advantage in sports such as sumo wrestling.

questions.q: Energy balance is achieved when:
options: Energy intake is greater than energy expenditure
Energy intake is less than energy expenditure
questions.explain: Energy balance occurs when the energy taken in from food equals the energy used by the body.

questions.q: If a performer regularly takes in more energy than they use, they will most likely:
questions.explain: A positive energy balance, where intake exceeds expenditure, leads to weight gain as energy is stored as fat.

questions.q: Obesity is best defined as:
options: Having a large amount of muscle
Having excess body fat to the extent that health may be affected
questions.explain: Obesity is an excessive accumulation of body fat that may negatively affect health.

questions.q: Which somatotype is muscular and broad-shouldered, often suited to power sports?
questions.explain: Mesomorphs are muscular, broad-shouldered and well suited to strength and power events.

questions.q: Dehydration during exercise is likely to cause:
options: The blood to thicken and performance to decline
questions.explain: Dehydration thickens the blood and reduces sweating, causing overheating and a drop in performance.

questions.q: Which somatotype is characterised by being lean, tall and thin with narrow shoulders?
questions.explain: Ectomorphs are typically tall, thin and lean with little muscle or fat.

questions.q: Which nutrient is most important for the growth and repair of muscle tissue?
questions.explain: Proteins provide amino acids needed for the growth and repair of body tissues including muscle.

questions.q: Which is a likely consequence of a sedentary lifestyle?
options: Increased risk of obesity and heart disease
questions.explain: A sedentary lifestyle increases the risk of obesity, high blood pressure and coronary heart disease.

questions.q: Fats are an important nutrient because they:
options: Provide a slow-release energy source and insulation
Cannot be stored by the body
questions.explain: Fats provide a concentrated, slow-release energy store and help insulate the body.

questions.q: A balanced diet for a performer should mainly consist of which macronutrient by proportion?
questions.explain: Carbohydrates should form the largest proportion of a balanced diet as they fuel activity.

questions.q: Why is hydration important for a performer?
options: It prevents a drop in performance and helps regulate body temperature
It removes the need for carbohydrates
questions.explain: Staying hydrated maintains blood volume and temperature control, preventing dehydration and a fall in performance.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of emotional health and well-being?
options: Having a strong heart and lungs
Making friends through a sports team
Being able to control emotions and feel relaxed
questions.explain: Emotional well-being relates to managing emotions, feeling confident and reducing stress.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes health and fitness?
options: Health is a state of complete well-being; fitness is the ability to meet the demands of the environment
Health only refers to physical strength
They mean exactly the same thing
Fitness includes mental health but health does not
questions.explain: Health is complete physical, mental and social well-being, while fitness is the ability to cope with the demands of activity.

questions.q: Which somatotype would generally be the greatest advantage for a long-distance runner?
questions.explain: An ectomorph's light, lean build is well suited to endurance events such as long-distance running.

questions.q: A marathon runner may 'carbo-load' before a race in order to:
questions.explain: Carbo-loading increases glycogen stores in the muscles, providing more energy for endurance events.
